title: Saved-sample timing and thermal response in invented histories

paragraphs.text: The invented histories separate saved-sample timing from thermal magnitude ({{figure:1}}). A first reaches the reporting threshold at {{value:A-crossing}} and has a saved maximum of {{value:A-max}} at {{value:A-peak}}, whereas B first satisfies the same threshold at {{value:B-crossing}} and reaches {{value:B-max}} at {{value:B-peak}}. Thus the later sampled threshold time in B accompanies a lower saved maximum in this illustrative pair. The time-weighted mean temperatures are {{value:A-mean}} and {{value:B-mean}}, respectively, distinguishing overall exposure from a single peak.

The saved heat-input histories differ in timing but have equal trapezoidal integrals, {{value:A-integral}} for A and {{value:B-integral}} for B. The separately supplied cumulative ledgers instead increase by {{value:A-ledger}} and {{value:B-ledger}} ({{table:1}}). The close but unequal ledger values are deliberately invented independently of the saved-rate reconstruction. This comparison separates cumulative accounting from quadrature of an instantaneous rate; it does not supply a complete energy balance.

Equal reconstructed heat input does not determine the temperature-peak ordering in these records. Relating that ordering to storage or transport would require a physical model and matched controls that are absent from this teaching dataset. The supported reading is therefore the joint temporal and thermal comparison, not a causal material ranking.

captions.1: Invented nonuniform thermal histories on a shared observed 0–12 s window. (a) Domain-maximum temperature, with the 400 K tutorial reporting level; markers are saved samples and straight segments guide the eye. Threshold times are first qualifying saved samples, not native events or interpolated crossings. (b) Instantaneous domain-integrated heat-input rate. (c) Independently supplied cumulative heat ledgers (solid lines with markers) and cumulative trapezoidal reconstructions of the saved rates (dashed lines). The cumulative ledger is not integrated again; no storage or boundary-loss channels are supplied.
